source.title: Towards scientific discovery with dictionary learning: Extracting biological concepts from microscopy foundation models
source.authors: Konstantin Donhauser; Kristina Ulicna; Gemma E. Moran; Aditya Ravuri; Kian Kenyon-Dean; Cian Eastwood; Jason Hartford

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates sparse dictionary features in microscopy foundation models and finds that they do not preserve all linearly available biological information, qualifying claims that such features are complete units. It does not test the original toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses the superposition hypothesis and reports results on sparse features learned from microscopy MAEs. Its biological feature results are not evidence about LLMs. The text also gives comparisons of ICFL and TopK SAE, PCA whitening, sparsity, and linear probing; only the TopK SAE reconstruction results are linked to V5 below. Results cited from other work were not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse dictionaries (ICFL and TopK SAE) on a 1.9B microscopy ViT-MAE. It probes the reconstructions against the original representation and concludes the features are 'clearly incomplete' on subtle-morphology tasks. That bears on the completeness part of V5, in a new (vision, non-LLM) setting. No other version is tested: there are no toy models, no polysemanticity-cause analysis, no LLMs and no multi-dimensional feature analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that dictionary learning extracts biologically interpretable features from microscopy MAEs, but the features are clearly incomplete: probe performance drops significantly on subtle-morphology tasks. They are unsure whether this comes from the DL method, model scale, or non-linear representation of such changes. They also find that ICFL and PCA whitening improve selectivity over TopK SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper learns sparse dictionaries for microscopy MAE representations using ICFL and compares with TopK SAEs; it does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments or their geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature quality and results vary with dictionary-learning method (ICFL versus TopK SAE), PCA whitening, sparsity, model size, and representation source (residual stream versus attention output). The text also reports that TopK SAE with PCA whitening has high reconstruction instability and that learning-rate effects differ by method.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse dictionary features from microscopy MAEs are selective for cell types, batches and perturbations (Table 2 counts). They correlate with CellProfiler selectivity (r=0.71), and token heatmaps recall 87.1% of expert-labelled control-like cells.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary learning recovers biologically interpretable features from non-language vision foundation models.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A: perturbation concepts are as linearly decodable from the encoder-decoder null-space component as from the full token. The row-space component gives lower accuracy, below even a random subspace of equal dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ViT-MAEs store abstract concepts linearly in a 'register'-like subspace not passed to the decoder.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The study is in microscopy vision models rather than LLMs or toy networks. The key linear-probing reconstruction values in Figure 4 are not stated numerically in the text, and the study does not test feature stability or canonicality. The biological feature assessments include qualitative interpretation; the single-cell quantitative check uses five images.
record.rows_left_out: Additional ablations and plots in Figures 8, 9, and 17–19 compare selectivity, reconstruction, model size, and representation source. They are not separately extracted here because the reported plotted values are not stated numerically in the text and the TopK SAE linear-probe task rows most directly bear on the tested V5 completeness question.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, no sparsity-dependent transition, no geometry.
All of it: no analysis of capacity or of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All of it: no study of why neurons are polysemantic.
The version is about LLMs; the study uses microscopy ViT-MAEs only. Its finding that sparse features are recoverable in MAEs is a different system.
Stability across seeds or runs, and canonicality or uniqueness of individual dictionary features, are not tested. Only information completeness via linear probing is tested.
All of it: features are assumed to be 1-D directions, with no comparison to multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Linear-probe BTA on reconstructions without PCA whitening: a clear drop for both ICFL and TopK.
Probe accuracy on reconstructions as a function of sparsity for task 5: it improves with more non-zeros, but less than whitening does.
Model-size ablation: MAE-L gives lower reconstruction probe accuracy on tasks 3 and 5 than MAE-G.

TopK SAE dead features: 7640 of 8192 without whitening and 8026 with it (ICFL: 55 and 341). TopK also shows training instability with whitening. Both bear on how usable and stable SAE dictionaries are.

record.verdict_notes: V5 is tested only for information completeness, and in a vision MAE rather than an LLM. r1–r5 should name ICFL as the default dictionary, and their baselines can be filled from Table 2. The reader's labels were inverted: r1/r2/r4 show near-complete retention (supports), and r3/r5 show partial retention (limits_scope, not challenges, since signal is substantially preserved).

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from limited capacity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Polysemantic neurons arising for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The claim concerns LLMs; the study examines microscopy vision MAEs, not language models.
The study tests information retention for TopK SAE reconstructions, but not the stability or canonicality of individual SAE features.
The study represents learned features as directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.
